Report_ID: Continuous smoking abstinence at 1 year (longest follow-up ≥6 months)
Title: Bupropion for Smoking Cessation in Patients With Acute Coronary Syndrome
Author: Planer et al.
Comment: Event counts not reported verbatim; derived from the paper's stated percentages applied to the randomised numbers from the Figure 1 flow diagram (0.31×75=23.25→23; 0.33×76=25.08→25), per the synthesis plan's percentage-to-count rule with ITT (2 participants lost to follow-up counted as smoking). Abstinence was self-reported continuous abstinence, not biochemically validated.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Bupropion hydrochloride SR 150 mg twice daily for 2 months + nurse-led counselling') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Study Environment: hospital inpatient with post-discharge telephone follow-up
Participant type: Hospitalised adult smokers with acute coronary syndrome (>10 cigarettes/day, intending to quit)
Recruitment source: Two campuses of Hadassah Medical Center, Jerusalem, Israel (inpatients)
Outcome measurement: Number of participants continuously abstinent / number randomised per arm (events derived from reported percentages: 31% of 75 ≈ 23; 33% of 76 ≈ 25)
Outcome variable: Continuous smoking abstinence at 1 year (longest follow-up ≥6 months)
outcome_family: smoking abstinence at longest follow-up of at least 6 months

Report_ID: Smoking abstinence at 12 months (continuous abstinence, biochemically validated)
Title: Bupropion for Smokers Hospitalized with Acute Cardiovascular Disease
Author: Rigotti NA, Thorndike AN, Regan S, et al.
Comment: Same participants as the primary 7-day point-prevalence row (duplicate sample) — only one of the two 12-month rows should be pooled. ITT denominators 124 vs 123 per Table 2 header (1 placebo death excluded from efficacy analyses).; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Sustained-release bupropion 300 mg/day for 12 weeks + cognitive-behavioural counselling') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Participant type: Adult smokers hospitalized with acute cardiovascular disease (primarily myocardial infarction and unstable angina)
Recruitment source: Five hospitals in Massachusetts and Maine, USA (inpatients)
Outcome measurement: Continuous abstinence: 7-day point prevalence abstinence at 2 weeks, 4 weeks, 3 months and 12 months, validated by expired air CO (2, 4 weeks) and saliva cotinine (3, 12 months)
Outcome variable: Smoking abstinence at 12 months (continuous abstinence, biochemically validated)
outcome_family: smoking abstinence at longest follow-up of at least 6 months

Report_ID: Continuous abstinence at 12 months (strictest definition, biochemically validated, ITT)
Title: Bupropion for Smoking Cessation in Patients Hospitalized With Acute Myocardial Infarction: A Randomized, Placebo-Controlled Trial (ZESCA)
Author: Eisenberg MJ
Comment: Event counts are NOT printed verbatim in the paper; they were derived from the reported percentages (26.8% and 22.2%) applied to the randomised arm sizes stated in Table 1 / Figure 1 (bupropion n=192, placebo n=200), per the synthesis plan's ITT denominator rule: 0.268*192=51.5 -> 51; 0.222*200=44.4 -> 44. Note the paper's own Figure 2 footnote gives 12-month "patient numbers" of 183 (bupropion) and 194 (placebo) ("includes all patients except those who died"); 49/183=26.8% and 43/194=22.2% reproduce the published percentages exactly, so the figure percentages were most likely computed on those death-excluded denominators. Only the percentages and p value are verbatim.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ("Bupropion SR 150 mg/day x3 days then 150 mg twice daily for 9 weeks + low-intensity 5A's counseling") is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Participant type: Hospitalized adult smokers (>=10 cigarettes/day) with enzyme-positive acute myocardial infarction
Outcome measurement: Number of participants continuously abstinent at 12 months, derived from reported percentages applied to randomised arm sizes
Outcome variable: Continuous abstinence at 12 months (strictest definition, biochemically validated, ITT)
outcome_family: smoking abstinence at longest follow-up of at least 6 months
